searchDocs.title: replicator​
searchDocs.content: </> SavedSource:replicator( valueType: GreenTeaType, lookup: (savedData: D) → T, incrementalConfig: SavedIncrementalConfig<T,P>? ) → SavedReplicator<D,T,P> Creates a SavedReplicator for the part of the saved data that lookup returns. The saved data passed to lookup is fully typed from the source's GreenTea type. researchReplicator = PlayerDataSource:replicator(gt.array(gt.string()), function(playerData) return playerData.research end), lookup must return an existing table from the saved data, or a primitive, and must not yield. Changes are found by comparing what it returns, so a lookup that builds a new table counts as changed on every save.

searchDocs.title: setFetchFunction​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> SavedSource:setFetchFunction(fetchAsync: (player: Player ) → D?) → () Sets the function that returns a player's saved data, yielding until it has loaded, or nil if it never loads. Replicators from this source wait for it to be set. PlayerDataSource:setFetchFunction(function(player) local didLoad, playerData = PlayerDataServer.waitForPlayerData(player) return if didLoad then playerData else nil end)

searchDocs.title: replicateChanges​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> SavedSource:replicateChanges( player: Player , newData: D, oldData: D? ) → () Tells the source that a player's saved data changed, including when it first loads (oldData is nil). Each replicator whose part changed sends it to the player, then fires its onChanged. Call it from your store's change callback. PlayerDataSource:replicateChanges(player, newData, oldData)

searchDocs.title: get​
searchDocs.content: </> TemporaryGlobalReplicator:get() → T Returns the current value without yielding. On the client, errors if the value hasn't arrived yet. Call Sencha.waitForReplicators while loading, or use TemporaryGlobalReplicator:getAsync or TemporaryGlobalReplicator:observe in code that may run earlier.

searchDocs.title: getAsync​
searchDocs.content: This is a yielding function. When called, it will pause the Lua thread that called the function until a result is ready to be returned, without interrupting other scripts. Yields </> TemporaryGlobalReplicator:getAsync() → T Returns the current value, yielding until it's available. The server value always exists, so it only yields on the client.

searchDocs.title: set​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> TemporaryGlobalReplicator:set(value: T) → () Sets the value and sends it to every player. Errors if the value doesn't match the replicator's type. Setting a primitive to the value it already has does nothing; setting a table always counts as a change.

searchDocs.title: applyIncrementalUpdate​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> TemporaryGlobalReplicator:applyIncrementalUpdate(patch: P) → () Applies patch to the value with the incremental config's apply, then sends only the patch to every player. Errors if the patch or the new value doesn't match its type, or if the replicator has no incremental config. An empty table patch does nothing.

searchDocs.title: onChanged​
searchDocs.content: </> TemporaryGlobalReplicator:onChanged(callback: ( newValue: T, oldValue: T ) → ()) → Disconnect Calls callback when the value changes, not for the initial value. On the server, the change is sent to clients before callback runs, so anything it changes in response reaches clients after the change that caused it.

searchDocs.title: observe​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client </> TemporaryGlobalReplicator:observe(callback: (value: T) → ()) → Disconnect Calls callback with the current value right away if it has arrived (otherwise when it arrives), then on every change.

searchDocs.title: onUpdateReceived​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client </> TemporaryGlobalReplicator:onUpdateReceived(callback: ( newValue: T, oldValue: T, patch: P ) → ()) → Disconnect Calls callback for each patch received, after the value is updated. Only replicators with an incremental config receive patches; calling this on one without errors. Full values (the first value, a set, or a resync) only fire TemporaryGlobalReplicator:onChanged, so use that to see every change.

searchDocs.title: getObservable​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client </> TemporaryGlobalReplicator:getObservable() → ObservableValue<T> Returns an ObservableValue that follows the replicated value, for code that works with ObservableValues, like the ReactObservableValue hooks. Calling it again returns the same one. Setting it doesn't change the replicated value. Errors if the value hasn't arrived yet. local isMeteorShower = ReactObservableValue.useObservableValue(EventsNetwork.meteorShowerReplicator:getObservable())

searchDocs.title: rateLimit​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the server. Server </> EventSwitchboard:rateLimit(limit: Limit) → EventSwitchboard Sets the rate limit for calls to each port from each player, replacing the default of 60 at once and 30 per second. Returns the same switchboard, so it can be chained where it's created. Errors if the limit is invalid. shopSwitchboard = Sencha.eventSwitchboard(gt.number()):rateLimit({ burst = 5, perSecond = 2 }),

searchDocs.title: Disconnect​
searchDocs.content: </> type Disconnect = () → () Every listener method returns a Disconnect, the cleanup function. Call it to stop listening. It's safe to call more than once, and can be handed to a cleanup library or returned from a React effect.

searchDocs.title: Limit​
searchDocs.content: </> interface Limit { burst: number-- calls a player can make at once; at least 1 perSecond: number-- calls a player gets back each second; more than 0 } A rate limit for calls from clients, passed to :rateLimit(...) on any remote. Each player has their own budget.

searchDocs.title: TemporaryIncrementalConfig​
searchDocs.content: </> interface TemporaryIncrementalConfig { patchType: GreenTeaType-- the GreenTea type of a patch apply: ( value: T, patch: P ) → T-- returns the value with the patch applied; runs on the server and the client } Makes a temporary replicator send patches with applyIncrementalUpdate instead of sending the whole value.

searchDocs.title: SavedIncrementalConfig​
searchDocs.content: </> interface SavedIncrementalConfig { patchType: GreenTeaType-- the GreenTea type of a patch diff: ( newValue: T, oldValue: T ) → P-- returns a patch describing what changed; runs on the server apply: ( value: T, patch: P ) → T-- returns the value with the patch applied; runs on the server and the client } Makes a saved replicator send patches instead of the whole value when the saved data changes.

searchDocs.title: temporaryReplicator​
searchDocs.content: </> Sencha.temporaryReplicator: { player: ( valueType, defaultValue, incrementalConfig? ) → TemporaryPlayerReplicator, global: ( valueType, initialValue, incrementalConfig? ) → TemporaryGlobalReplicator } Creates replicators for state the server keeps in memory. temporaryReplicator.player creates a [TemporaryPlayerReplicator]: one value per player, sent only to that player. temporaryReplicator.global creates a [TemporaryGlobalReplicator]: one value, sent to every player. carriedOreReplicator = Sencha.temporaryReplicator.player(gt.number(), 0), meteorShowerReplicator = Sencha.temporaryReplicator.global(gt.boolean(), false),

searchDocs.title: event​
searchDocs.content: </> Sencha.event( ...: GreenTeaType-- the type of each argument ) → Event<T...> Creates an Event, a typed RemoteEvent. Arguments are checked against the GreenTea types on both sides. damageEvent = Sencha.event(gt.number(), gt.Vector3()),

searchDocs.title: unreliableEvent​
searchDocs.content: </> Sencha.unreliableEvent( ...: GreenTeaType-- the type of each argument ) → Event<T...> Creates an Event backed by an UnreliableRemoteEvent. It has the same API as Sencha.event, but messages may be dropped or arrive out of order, and payloads are limited to roughly 900 bytes. Use it for repeating updates where only the latest matters, never for messages that must arrive.

searchDocs.content: </> Sencha.func( args: GreenTeaArgs,-- gt.args(...) returns: GreenTeaReturns-- gt.returns(...) ) → Function<T...,R...> Creates a Function, a typed RemoteFunction the client invokes on the server. buyItemRemote = Sencha.func(gt.args(gt.string()), gt.returns(gt.boolean())),

searchDocs.title: savedSource​
searchDocs.content: </> Sencha.savedSource( name: string,-- a name unique to this store savedDataType: GreenTeaType-- the built GreenTea type of the saved data ) → SavedSource<D> Creates a SavedSource for one store of saved player data. Create one per store in a shared module, then create replicators from it with SavedSource:replicator. -- ReplicatedStorage/PlayerDataSource.luau return Sencha.savedSource("PlayerData", PlayerDataTypes.PlayerData)

searchDocs.title: define​
searchDocs.content: </> Sencha.define( parent: Instance ,-- usually script implementations: T-- a table of remotes and replicators ) → T Names and sets up every remote and replicator in implementations from its key, and returns the same table. Remotes are created under parent, and each replicator's name is parent:GetFullName() plus its key, so the same module resolves to the same remotes and replicators on both sides. Each remote and replicator can only be defined once.

searchDocs.title: waitForReplicators​
searchDocs.content: This item only works when running on the client. Client This is a yielding function. When called, it will pause the Lua thread that called the function until a result is ready to be returned, without interrupting other scripts. Yields </> Sencha.waitForReplicators() → () Yields until every replicator the server has defined has its first value on this client, including ones whose modules the client hasn't required yet. After it returns, get() is safe on every replicator. Call it once while loading, before starting systems that read replicated values. If it's still waiting after 5 seconds it warns and lists what it's waiting on.

Each call spends one token and is checked once, however many listeners there are.
